sections.heading: La distinción esencial
sections.body: Los sustantivos contables (*countable nouns*) representan entidades individuales que se pueden enumerar y poseen formas singular y plural (*an apple, two apples*). Los sustantivos incontables (*uncountable nouns*) representan masas continuas, materiales o conceptos abstractos; no tienen forma plural en inglés y concuerdan con verbos en singular (*water, information, advice*).

sections.heading: Sustantivos incontables que confunden a hispanohablantes
sections.body: Muchos sustantivos que son contables en español son estrictamente incontables en inglés: **advice** (nunca 'an advice' ni 'advices'), **information** (nunca 'informations'), **furniture** (nunca 'furnitures'), **luggage / baggage**, **homework**, **news**, **weather**, **traffic**, **knowledge**.

sections.heading: Cuantificadores adecuados
sections.body: Solo para contables: *many, few, a few, several, a number of*. Solo para incontables: *much, little, a little, an amount of*. Válidos para ambos: *some, any, a lot of, plenty of, most*.

sections.heading: Partitivos y unidades de medida
sections.body: Para contar sustantivos incontables se recurre a palabras partitivas: *a piece of advice* (un consejo), *a piece of furniture* (un mueble), *two items of luggage* (dos piezas de equipaje), *a bottle of water* (una botella de agua).

examples.english: Can you give me some advice?
examples.note: No se dice 'an advice' ni 'some advices'.

examples.english: I need more information about the course.
We bought two pieces of furniture.
There's a lot of traffic on the highway today.
examples.note: 'Traffic' es incontable y lleva verbo en singular.

exercises.instruction: Clasifica cada sustantivo como contable (C) o incontable (U).

quiz.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct in English?
options: She gave me a good advice.
She gave me some good advices.
She gave me a piece of good advice.
quiz.explanation: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun. To refer to a single recommendation, use 'a piece of advice' or 'some advice'.

quiz.question: Which quantifier can be used with BOTH countable and uncountable nouns?
quiz.explanation: 'A lot of' works with both countable nouns ('a lot of books') and uncountable nouns ('a lot of water').
